verdict.rationale: Docs explicitly describe a learning loop where 👍/👎 reactions and reply comments train Greptile to stop repeating feedback team members don't want, with noise control filtering repetitive comments (greptile-docs-4, greptile-docs-33, greptile-docs-32). However, this is described as a team-wide, multi-week aggregate learning process rather than an immediate per-developer 'push back once and it never repeats' guarantee, and no independent/hands-on evidence confirms the mechanism works as described. Missing for 10: independent corroboration of the learning behavior, and clarity on whether a single developer's pushback (vs. team consensus over weeks) suppresses a specific rejected comment.
